proof_summary: For \(N=2\cdot100943\cdot3^{39101}-1\), modular exponentiation and gcd computations in \(\mathbb F_q[x]/(x^2-4x+1)\) show that, for any prime divisor \(q\mid N\), the class of \(x\) has exact order \(N+1\): its \((N+1)\)-st power is 1, while division of the exponent by each prime factor \(2,3,100943\) does not give 1. If \(N\) were composite and \(q\) its least prime factor, this order would force \(N+1<q^2\), contradicting \(q^2\le N\); hence \(N\) is prime, and the positive exponent \(39101\) supplies the required counterexample.
